title: Vital Signs, Weight, Height, Apex Beat and Fetal Heart Beat
path: Vital Signs, Weight, Height, Apex Beat and Fetal Heart Beat

headings.title: Introduction to Baseline Physical Measurements and Vital Signs
headings.content: Baseline measurements provide a numerical foundation for evaluating a patient's physical status upon admission to a ward or clinic in Nigeria. These metrics capture current physiological functioning and guide subsequent nursing interventions. Nurses obtain these values systematically to spot sudden deterioration or gradual recovery. Consistent recording creates a reliable trend line over the course of hospital admission.

headings.title: Core Vital Signs: Temperature, Pulse, Respiration, and Blood Pressure
headings.content:
Core vital signs reflect the body's most critical regulatory functions. 
- **Temperature**: Measures the body's thermal regulation, typically assessed via the axillary or tympanic route in routine ward settings.
- **Pulse**: Evaluates heart rate, rhythm, and volume, most commonly felt at the radial artery.
- **Respiration**: Counts the number of ventilation cycles per minute, observed discreetly to prevent the patient from altering their breathing pattern.
- **Blood Pressure**: Quantifies the lateral pressure exerted by circulating blood on arterial walls using a sphygmomanometer and stethoscope.

headings.title: Measuring Anthropometric Data: Weight and Height Techniques
headings.content: Anthropometric measurements quantify human physical dimensions to evaluate nutritional status and calculate medication dosages. Accurate weight measurement requires a calibrated scale with the patient wearing minimal clothing and no shoes. Height assessment utilizes a stadiometer, ensuring the patient stands upright with the head in the Frankfort horizontal plane. In resource-limited or emergency settings where patients cannot stand, recumbent length or proxy indicators like mid-upper arm circumference serve as alternatives.

headings.title: Assessing the Apex Beat: Location, Technique, and Clinical Significance
headings.content: The apex beat represents the point of maximal impulse created by the left ventricle striking the chest wall during systole. In healthy adults, it is typically located at the fifth left intercostal space along the midclavicular line. Nurses use the fingertips of the examining hand or the stethoscope diaphragm to palpate this impulse. A displaced apex beat often signals cardiac enlargement or heart failure, requiring prompt medical review.

headings.title: Obstetric Assessment: Locating and Monitoring the Fetal Heart Beat
headings.content: Monitoring the fetal heart beat is essential for assessing intrauterine well-being during pregnancy and labor. Healthcare providers utilize a Pinard stethoscope or an electronic Doppler ultrasound device. The location to place the instrument depends on the fetal lie, presentation, and position determined through Leopold's maneuvers. A normal baseline fetal heart rate ranges between 110 and 160 beats per minute.

headings.title: Documentation, Normal Ranges, and Clinical Interpretation
headings.content: Accurate documentation completes the assessment cycle and ensures continuity of care across different shifts. Nurses must record exact numerical values alongside the date and time in the patient's chart. Recognizing normal physiological parameters enables prompt identification of abnormal trends that require escalation to medical staff. Clear records protect patient safety and maintain legal standards of nursing practice.
